Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  June 5, 2025

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on June 5, 2025. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Octavio Padilla
  - District 2, Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4,
  Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director
  Mary Rouzan  Recreation Supervisor
  Baz Devlia  Human Services Superintendent
  Brian McClure  Parks Administration Superintendent
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner Padilla
that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on May 1, 2025, be
approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:
Ayes: Commissioners Denmon, Padilla, Beck, and Brown
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Parks Administration Superintendent Brian McClure
reported the following: Park Maintenance has begun renovations on the Manchester
Avenue median near the 405 off-ramp. With the 2026 World Cup, 2027 Super Bowl, and
2028 Olympics all taking place in Inglewood, this project is part of our early efforts to
beautify the city in preparation for these global events. This morning, the City opened the
bidding process to contract with a landscape company to maintain our medians and
parkways. Once awarded, this contract will allow our in-house crews to focus more of their

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

efforts on enhancing and maintaining our parks. Tree Maintenance staff is finalizing a
Request for Bids for a tree inventory and mapping project. The goal is to use GPS data to
identify and document over 1,500 trees located throughout our park system. Graffiti
Abatement – We apologize for not including our usual graffiti abatement graph this time.
We are still finalizing the data to ensure accuracy before sharing. We recently filled a
vacancy in the graffiti team by promoting one of our part-time employees to a full-time
position. The Graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739.
REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor Mary Rouzan reported the following:
Summer Camp – Swimming pool – Movies in the Park - The Parks, Recreation and
Community Services Department will return this summer with our annual Movies in the
Park series. This free summer event offers family-friendly outdoor movie screenings that
bring residents together for fun under the stars. Each movie night features a recently
released film, along with arts and crafts, games, food trucks, and complimentary popcorn.
In support of the City’s environmental goals, every screening includes a short video
promoting recycling and waste reduction. The 2025 Movies in the Park series will take place
on June 28 at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park with Mufasa, July 26 at Inglewood City Hall featuring
Moana 2, and August 16 at North Park showcasing Despicable Me 4. All movies are free and
begin at dusk. Food and refreshments will be available for purchase. We encourage you to
grab your blankets and lawn chairs and join us for an unforgettable evening at the cinema
under the stars. For more information on our Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city
sports website at: https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Superintendent Baz Devlia reported on the
following: Senior Center Operations - Senior Center Transportation the City of Inglewood’s
paratransit program continues to provide trips to seniors and the disabled community in
Inglewood and Hawthorne. We recently hired a full time bus operator who is quickly being
acclimated to his new paratransit service. In the coming weeks we expect to hire one (1)
part time bus operator to ensure we have ample bus operators to cover our paratransit
service. We are excited to bring on these two experienced bus operators to assist and
again, make immediate positive impacts on our service. As always, we look forward to
continuing to provide the best possible service for our seniors and disabled
community. Senior Nutrition Program serves approximately 470 seniors per week through
home delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate meals. We continue to offer
fresh produce weekly in partnership with the Social Justice Learning Institute, and monthly
shelf stable meal boxes in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank. Seniors enjoy
themselves and build lasting relationships with fellow seniors/staff, while our numbers
continue to climb weekly in program participation. Senior Center Activities our Senior
Center is experiencing significant growth, with notable increases in participations numbers
and an expanded range of programs. Grace Farwell of the organization Helping Elderly Live
Productively, or H.E.L.P. for short, will be presenting on the topic of helping seniors improve

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

their ability to do daily tasks and live independently on June 25. A new Monday and
Wednesday chair aerobics class started on May 28.
   Mercedes Aguirre of the LA County Department of Mental Health will be conducting
  a presentation on Managing your Medication on June 9.
   On June 12 we will be showing the movie “Pride & Prejudice”.
   On June 13 we will be having a Father’s Day celebration from 10:00 a.m. to 11:00
  a.m.
   A program has been planned to honor Juneteenth on Thursday, June 19, beginning
  at 10:00 a.m. - 11:30 a.m. There will be special performances by our Inspirational
  Choir, Inglewood Yola, and poetry reading.
   Opicacares will be presenting a caregiver resources presentation on June 25. On
  June 26 we will be having our dance party event from 2:00 p.m. To 4:00 p.m.
   July 3 will see our annual Independence Day party, including live entertainment,
  plenty of hot dogs, games, and dancing.
Child and Adult Care Food Program has finished for the fiscal year, and we are gearing up
to start our Summer Food Service Program. We will serve at six different locations for youth
18 and under. The sites are Ashwood Park, Crenshaw Library, Darby Park, Siminski Park,
Rogers Park, and Edward Jr. Vincent Park. We will be providing breakfast, Lunch, and snacks
at different sites and the times will vary according to the sites.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Department Director Thomas Uwal reported on the following:
FY2025-26 Budget Request Kick-Off all City departments are currently preparing their
budget requests for Fiscal Year 2025-2026. In alignment with this effort, our department
has submitted a comprehensive proposal outlining anticipated revenues and planned
expenditures for the upcoming year. This budget request document details our funding
allocations, program initiatives, policy proposals, and projected spending. It serves as a
roadmap for how we plan to utilize resources to support departmental goals and
community priorities in the year ahead. Inglewood Independence Day Music Festival will
commemorate Independence Day with a one-day music festival celebrating community
spirit and cultural diversity. The event will showcase performances from renowned artists
across a variety of music genres, including R&B, Old-School Rock, Latin, Jazz, and Hip-Hop.
In addition to live entertainment, the festival will feature an array of food and merchandise
vendors offering multicultural cuisine and distinctive goods such as jewelry, apparel, home
décor, barbecue, tacos, and refreshing beverages. The festival will take place on Saturday,
July 5, 2025, at Darby Park, located at 3400 Arbor Vitae Street, Inglewood, CA 90305. Storm
Water Community Meeting - The City of Inglewood is at 60% planning to design and
construct a multi-benefit storm water improvements project at Edward Vincent Jr. Park.
The primary goal of the project is to improve water quality in the downstream Centinela
Creek and Ballona Creek Estuary by capturing, treating, and infiltrating storm water.
Additional goals include enhancing park amenities at the project site for the community
and providing new educational opportunities. The City will facilitate community

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

involvement and participation during project development, seeking input on proposed
surface improvements. The City will also inform the neighborhood and interested parties
of the project status, including construction schedule and anticipated impacts and benefits.
The city is hosting community Meeting on June 16, 2025 from 6-8 PM at Veterans Memorial
Building; Edward Vincent Jr. Park 330 Centinela Ave. Inglewood, CA 90302. We encourage
everyone to participate at the meeting to give their feedback.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Padilla complimented the Touch a Truck
event and the Little League closing ceremony on being a success.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:46 p.m.
